Rates of trait evolution from the trophic level of each lineage in a food web

Source: R/traits_rates.R
food_web_rates.Rd

Turns the rates of change of the mean traits of the resource, the consumer and the predator in food_web_dynamics() into rates of evolution of a continuous trait on the branches of a tree whose tips belong to these levels, for trait_rates(edge_rates = ). It implements the expectation that lineages at different trophic positions evolve at different speeds, and that the rates change when a level is added (scenario 4 of the notes on branch rates).

Usage

food_web_rates(x, tree, levels, sigma2 = 1, k = 1, window = NULL)

Arguments

x

Result of food_web_dynamics().

tree

A tree of class phylo.

levels

Trophic level of each tip, "R", "N" or "P", named by tip label or in the order of tree$tip.label.

sigma2

Rate outside the stretch informed by the metacommunity.

k

Increase of the rate, relative to sigma2, per unit of speed (trait units per unit of time of the food web).

window

Length of the end of each tip branch represented by the metacommunity, in the units of the branch lengths; NULL uses the whole tip branch. A window longer than a tip branch is cut to its length.

Value

Numeric vector with the rate of each branch, in the order of the rows of tree$edge, with the speed of each level as attribute "speed".

Details

The speed of a level is the mean of its rate of trait change, \(|d\bar z / dt|\), over the steps at which it is present. Like turnover_rates(), the food web runs in ecological time and only informs the tip branches: over the last window units of time of each tip branch the rate is \(\mathrm{sigma2}\, (1 + k \cdot \mathrm{speed})\) of the level of the tip, and elsewhere it is sigma2. These speeds are directional changes of the mean trait under selection, not the variance per unit time of Brownian motion, so they give relative rates among levels, scaled by k, not an equivalence between the two.

References

McPeek, M. A. (2017). Evolutionary Community Ecology. Princeton University Press. doi:10.23943/princeton/9780691088778.001.0001

See also

food_web_dynamics(), turnover_rates(), trait_rates()

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), plot_traits(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), species_traits(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_mk(), trait_ou(), trait_rates(), turnover_rates()

Examples

set.seed(1)
web <- food_web_dynamics(seq(0, 4000, by = 20), init = c(R = 50, N = 0.1, P = 0.1),
                         traits = c(R = 10, N = 4, P = 6), introductions = c(P = 2000),
                         dt = 0.5)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(9)
levels <- rep(c("R", "N", "P"), each = 3)
# speeds are small (trait units per time step), so k is large
rates <- food_web_rates(web, tr, levels, k = 500)
attr(rates, "speed")
#>           R           N           P 
#> 0.001989566 0.002973562 0.000143305 
x <- trait_rates(tr, edge_rates = rates)
